claims.text: The structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoparticles from 473 to 1923 K is governed by competition between configurational entropy and lattice-distortion-induced kinetic barriers.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous solid solution at lower temperatures.
Significant lattice distortion restricts atomic diffusion.
Restricted atomic diffusion caused by lattice distortion delays phase segregation at elevated temperatures.
Substituting constituent metals with elements having substantially different atomic radii increases lattice distortion while equiatomic ratios are retained.
Metals with similar atomic radii produce a minimal-lattice-distortion control.
Increasing temperature enables diffusion-driven atomic rearrangement in high-entropy materials.
High-entropy alloys can exhibit chemical clustering, short-range ordering, or decomposition as composition and temperature vary.
Elemental substitution can alter phase stability and the length scale of decomposition in a high-entropy alloy.
Nanoparticles with enhanced lattice distortion will retain a homogeneous solid solution to higher temperatures than minimal-distortion controls.
Enhanced lattice distortion will produce a delayed onset of phase segregation or chemical inhomogeneity within 473–1923 K.
Oxidation, departures from equiatomic composition, and nanoparticle-size effects may confound the relationship between lattice distortion and stability.
The prediction is conditional on controlled synthesis, uniform nanoparticle-size distributions, and identical thermal treatments.
A similar or earlier phase-change onset in the enhanced-distortion samples relative to the control would falsify the proposed stabilizing role of lattice-distortion-induced kinetic barriers.

contradictions.description: The design calls the two sets chemically identical in overall equiatomic composition while also requiring one set to contain substituted elements. Both sets can individually be equiatomic, but they cannot have identical elemental compositions if constituents are replaced.
